editorial:
Imagine being a tiny kid in a world where adults are mostly mean and you have nothing to your name. You get thrown into this gritty version of old London where a simple request for more food gets you kicked out of the orphanage. You quickly meet the Artful Dodger, a fast-talking street kid who leads you straight into the hands of Fagin, a grumpy old man who teaches homeless kids how to pick pockets. The vibe is dark and foggy, making you feel like you are right there in the muddy streets with Oliver, just hoping someone kind will finally show up.

What really works here is the tension. Bill Sikes is a scary villain who keeps you on edge every time he appears on screen. While the pace is a bit slower than modern movies, the acting is top-notch and the sets look incredibly real. If you enjoy classic stories about underdogs beating the odds, you will love this. For the best experience, try renting it on Apple TV or adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection so you can see all those detailed shots of the city in high quality.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head when Bill Sikes tries to run away after his crimes. He ends up accidentally hanging himself while trying to escape over a roof. Fagin is eventually caught by the police and sent to be executed. Oliver finally finds out the truth about his family and discovers he comes from a wealthy background. Mr. Brownlow officially adopts him, giving the boy the loving home and safety he always wanted.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves timeless stories about overcoming hardship.
